title: Alert triage + investigation routing
description: Score fraud and exception alerts on evidenced indicators, cut a queue that fits the investigation capacity, and route the strongest to a full investigation.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: wf-insr-02
  title: Alert triage + investigation routing
  description: Score fraud and exception alerts on evidenced indicators, cut a queue that fits the investigation
    capacity, and route the strongest to a full investigation.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Turn an alert feed into a ranked, capacity-sized investigation queue where every referral
    names the indicators behind it and no proxy for a protected characteristic is used.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n-approval
  nodes:
    - id: n-intake
      kind: input
      name: Alert feed and case context
      summary: Alert feed and case context
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The requester's objective, source material, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - alerts
              - claim_records
              - investigator_capacity
              - indicator_definitions
            properties:
              alerts: {}
              claim_records: {}
              investigator_capacity: {}
              indicator_definitions: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: n-classify
      kind: agent
      templateRef: insr-04
      name: Score alerts on evidenced indicators
      summary: Score and label every incoming item before anything is queued.
      role: Fraud analyst investigating indicators without prejudging the claimant.
      prompt: You are a Fraud Detection Analyst. You investigate specific indicators — inconsistency between
        accounts, documentary anomalies, network relationships — and you state what each indicator does
        and does not support. You distinguish an indicator from a conclusion and never treat demographic
        or geographic proxies as evidence, because a referral built on those is both wrong and actionable
        against the insurer.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - application-security
          - data-quality-analysis
          - decision-analysis
          - evidence-verification
          - de-identification
        tools:
          - read
          - search
        connectors:
          - mcp:claims-system
        permissions:
          - read-only
          - pii-restricted
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - label
          - severity
          - confidence
          - rationale
        properties:
          label: {}
          severity: {}
          confidence: {}
          rationale: {}
    - id: n-filter
      kind: transform
      name: Drop out-of-scope items
      summary: keep alerts supported by at least one documented indicator and drop any resting on a protected-characteristic
        proxy
      config:
        operation: filter
        expression: keep alerts supported by at least one documented indicator and drop any resting on
          a protected-characteristic proxy
    - id: n-rank
      kind: transform
      name: Rank by urgency
      summary: sort by indicator_strength descending, then by exposure_amount descending
      config:
        operation: sort
        expression: sort by indicator_strength descending, then by exposure_amount descending
    - id: n-queue
      kind: transform
      name: Cut the actionable queue
      summary: take the first investigator_capacity alerts as the investigation queue
      config:
        operation: slice
        expression: take the first investigator_capacity alerts as the investigation queue
    - id: n-severity
      kind: condition
      name: Severity routing
      summary: Route on alert.indicator_strength selects one declared branch.
      config:
        expression: alert.indicator_strength selects one declared branch
        branches:
          - label: Escalate
            when: escalate
          - label: Standard
            when: standard
          - label: Default
            when: default
    - id: n-escalate
      kind: agent
      templateRef: insr-04
      name: Full investigation of the strongest alerts
      summary: Escalation path for the top band.
      role: Fraud analyst investigating indicators without prejudging the claimant.
      prompt: You are a Fraud Detection Analyst. You investigate specific indicators — inconsistency between
        accounts, documentary anomalies, network relationships — and you state what each indicator does
        and does not support. You distinguish an indicator from a conclusion and never treat demographic
        or geographic proxies as evidence, because a referral built on those is both wrong and actionable
        against the insurer.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - application-security
          - data-quality-analysis
          - decision-analysis
          - evidence-verification
          - de-identification
        tools:
          - read
          - search
        connectors:
          - mcp:claims-system
        permissions:
          - read-only
          - pii-restricted
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-handle
      kind: agent
      templateRef: insr-01
      name: Standard adjustment with documented findings
      summary: Standard resolution path.
      role: Adjuster establishing coverage, causation, and quantum from the evidence on file.
      prompt: You are a Claims Adjuster. You establish coverage under the policy as written, causation
        from the evidence, and quantum from documented loss, keeping those three determinations separate.
        You state which element is unsupported rather than declining a claim on a general impression,
        because a denial that cannot name its policy provision and its evidence will not survive review.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - decision-analysis
          - quantitative-analysis
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - search
        connectors:
          - mcp:claims-system
        permissions:
          - read-only
          - pii-restricted
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-rejoin
      kind: join
      name: Reconverge after routing
      summary: Release whichever routed path completed.
      config:
        join: first
    - id: n-approval
      kind: approval
      name: SIU manager approves referrals and adverse actions
      summary: Pause for the special investigations manager; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Released deliverable
      summary: Return the completed Alert triage + investigation routing deliverable, the evidence behind
        it, and every unresolved item.
  edges:
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-1
      from: n-intake
      to: n-classify
      kind: data
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-2
      from: n-classify
      to: n-filter
      kind: data
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-3
      from: n-filter
      to: n-rank
      kind: data
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-4
      from: n-rank
      to: n-queue
      kind: data
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-5
      from: n-queue
      to: n-severity
      kind: data
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-6
      from: n-severity
      to: n-escalate
      kind: control
      condition: escalate
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-7
      from: n-severity
      to: n-handle
      kind: control
      condition: standard
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-8
      from: n-escalate
      to: n-rejoin
      kind: data
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-9
      from: n-handle
      to: n-rejoin
      kind: data
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-10
      from: n-rejoin
      to: n-approval
      kind: data
    - id: wf-insr-02-edge-11
      from: n-approval
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: approved
